To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a higher order of quadrature formulae for the contact integral in a subdomain approach and the application of a higher order finite element interpolation in the computations are essential to achieve a good convergence of the solution.

the contact algorithms are robust and efficient, the convergence of the solution can be improved by using higher order quadrature rules, the order of the finite element interpolation is not important, and finally the algorithms are suitable for frictional contact problems.

a) the contact integral and the contact tangent matrices can be evaluated by a subdomain integration procedure and b) the order of the finite element interpolation used for the discretization of the contact surface and the rigid surface, respectively, has a significant influence on the accuracy of the contact solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an efficient and robust contact algorithm for sheet metal forming problems, which is applicable for large deformation analysis.
the numerical aspects of the contact algorithms and their influence on the accuracy and the computational time.
a new class of contact elements for large deformation contact analysis with the so-called ''Solid-Shell'' elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented algorithms are suitable for the simulation of sheet metal forming processes with high stretching and local contact pressure.
for a reliable and efficient solution of contact problems the use of a higher order of the finite element interpolation and a higher order of integration formula is necessary.
for the problems under consideration the penalty approach works very well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a very efficient contact formulation is available which can be used for a large variety of contact problems.
we have found a way to solve large deformation contact problems using 'Solid- Shell' elements.
the presented approach is able to solve large deformation contact problems with high stretching, which is a common problem in the forming industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a subdomain integration method is very efficient for contact problems in the case of large deformation and high contact pressure.
for a large class of problems a subdomain integration of contact elements is sufficient.
the proposed contact elements can be applied to a broad range of problems in sheet metal forming.
